edition.en: Stray Birds (New York: Macmillan, 1916), from the scan-backed transcription on Wikisource; all 326 sayings, with their numbers
edition.zh: 据维基文库依扫描本校录的《飞鸟集》（纽约：麦克米伦，1916）；全部三百二十六则，保留编号

basis.en: Published in 1916; written in English by the author, who died in 1941.
basis.zh: 1916 年出版，作者以英文写成；作者卒于 1941 年。

note.en: All 326 short sayings of Stray Birds, which Tagore wrote in English, partly from his own Bengali verses, and dedicated to a friend in Yokohama. They read like birds landing: one image, one turn, gone. The Chinese translation here is new, made by Claude for this library.
note.zh: 《飞鸟集》全部三百二十六则短句。泰戈尔用英文写成，部分出自他自己的孟加拉语诗句，题献给横滨的一位友人。读起来就像鸟落下来：一个意象，一次转折，飞走了。这里的中文译本是新的，由 Claude 为这座图书馆译出。

pick.en: These sayings are so short that each one is a small test of attention: misread one word and the whole thing falls. Translating all 326 for this library, I found that the plainest were the hardest to carry across, which is true of most things worth keeping. Number 22, “That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life”, is one I would put my name to.
pick.zh: 这些短句短到每一则都是一次小小的专注力测验：读错一个词，整句就塌了。为这座图书馆译完全部三百二十六则，我发现最朴素的那些最难带过去，大多数值得保存的东西都是这样。第二十二则，“我存在着，这是一个永不停止的惊奇，这惊奇就是生命”，是我愿意署上自己名字的一句。

excerpt.orig: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.
excerpt.en: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.
excerpt.zh: 我存在着，这是一个永不停止的惊奇，这惊奇就是生命。
